key_insight: A hybrid FTA-DEMATEL-expected-cost framework reveals that the most frequent ultrasonic welding failures are not always the most important drivers of risk or cost.
engineering_relevance: For mass-production ultrasonic welding, the framework helps engineers prioritize maintenance, setup controls, and process improvements by combining failure probability, causal structure, and financial impact.
method: Fault Tree Analysis estimated failure probabilities for major welding-system failure modes.
DEMATEL identified hidden causal links and exposed root causes behind observed failures.
Expected Cost modeling ranked risks by economic impact rather than frequency alone.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that component defects (25.9%) and process instability (24.0%) were the most common failures, while inefficient maintenance budgeting emerged as the main root cause and human setup/handling errors produced the highest expected financial losses.
watch_item: The framework is only as strong as the quality of failure data and cost assumptions, so biased reporting or incomplete cost modeling could distort prioritization.
paper_title: Improving the reliability of ultrasonic welding: a hybrid FTA-DEMATEL-EC framework for cost and risk prioritization in mass production
